g10-history-uh7-t1.overview: Rise of Independent States in Africa sits inside Africa Since 1960. National liberation movements swept across Africa after 1960, the focus of Unit 7 of Grade 10 History in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, it follows the rise of independent states in north, west, east, and southern Africa. Then it explains apartheid in South Africa and the struggle of the ANC. Next, it covers Pan-Africanism, the OAU, and the later African Union. Also it looks at the struggle for economic independence and regional communities. Finally, it examines major issues such as ethnic conflict, poverty, and population growth. Students will also learn how national liberation applies to real-life situations, such as unity and development in Africa today.
objectives: Compare the forms of national liberation struggle across Africa.
Explain apartheid and the struggle that ended it in South Africa.
Describe Pan-Africanism and the work of the OAU.
Assess the successes and failures of African regional communities.
Analyse the major challenges facing independent African states.
g10-history-uh7-t1.simple:
Rise of Independent States in Africa in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, national liberation in North Africa, from Egypt and Libya to Algeria’s war.
  • Independence in British and French West Africa, led by Nkrumah and others.
  • Also East and Central Africa, including Kenya’s Mau Mau and the Congo crisis.
  • Guerrilla wars against Portuguese and settler rule in southern Africa.
g10-history-uh7-t1.detailed:
Rise of Independent States in Africa — the essentials. First, national liberation in North Africa, from Egypt and Libya to Algeria’s war. Independence in British and French West Africa, led by Nkrumah and others. Also East and Central Africa, including Kenya’s Mau Mau and the Congo crisis. Guerrilla wars against Portuguese and settler rule in southern Africa.

What the MoE expects you to be able to do:

  • Compare the forms of national liberation struggle across Africa.
  • Explain apartheid and the struggle that ended it in South Africa.
  • Describe Pan-Africanism and the work of the OAU.
  • Assess the successes and failures of African regional communities.
  • Analyse the major challenges facing independent African states.
